md_description: This workflow captures purification and screening of monoclonal antibodies against cancer cell antigens. It includes cell preparation, ELISA and flow cytometry binding measurements, and apoptosis/proliferation functional assays. The resulting derived metrics are integrated into a final prioritization table for selecting lead antibody candidates for further development as immunotherapeutic agents.

hybridoma_culture.reasoning: The hybridoma_culture node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic identity/origin fields for the live hybridoma culture that are needed to understand what biological source produced the antibodies. I excluded any collection, purification, assay, capture, signal, or derivative fields because those belong to downstream Process/Capture/Signal nodes. I also avoided experiment-wide identifiers because the instructions state sample/subject/experiment identifiers are generated once at the root Entity node and should not be repeated. No already_generated fields were provided, so there was no overlap to resolve.

md_schema.descr: Stable identifier for the hybridoma clone or cell line producing the monoclonal antibody, recorded at culture registration before supernatant collection; example format: HBM-00123.
Identifier for the immunogen, antigen, or target cell preparation used to generate the hybridoma, recorded as the biological origin of the clone; example format: AGN-CA125-01.
Antibody class/subclass secreted by the hybridoma culture, determined from the producing clone's intrinsic product profile; common examples include IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b, IgG3, IgM, IgA.
Species from which the hybridoma was derived, reported for the cell source before any purification or assay steps; typical values in this workflow are mouse or rat.
Myeloma or fusion partner cell line used to create the hybridoma, recorded as an intrinsic origin attribute of the culture; example format: SP2/0-Ag14 or P3X63Ag8.653.
Source tissue or anatomical origin of the B-cell donor used for hybridoma generation, if applicable; example values include spleen, lymph node, or peripheral blood.

Primary antigen or cell-surface target recognized by the hybridoma-derived antibody, described as the intended biological binding target before screening measurements; example format: HER2, EGFR, CD20, or tumor-associated antigen name.

Whether the hybridoma material represented here is a live maintenance culture, a frozen stock, or an actively expanded culture at the time this entity is defined; captures the biological state of the source material, not the collection protocol.

antibody_supernatant.reasoning: The antibody_supernatant node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the collected culture fluid itself: what it is, how it is identified, and compositional/quality attributes that belong to the material prior to purification. I excluded collection protocol settings, collection duration, centrifugation, storage conditions, and downstream purification details because those belong to the culture_collection Process or antibody_purification Process. I also avoided repeating any sample-level identifiers that would already be assigned at the root Entity node in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the collected culture-fluid aliquot containing secreted monoclonal antibodies; example format: SUP-0001.
Identifier of the hybridoma clone that secreted the antibodies present in this supernatant, recorded as the biological source of the collected fluid; example format: HBM-00123.
Date when the antibody-containing culture fluid was harvested from the hybridoma culture, recorded as a material-origin attribute of the supernatant; ISO format example: 2026-08-18.
Total volume of harvested culture fluid associated with this entity, measured after collection and before purification; typical range in screening workflows is 1-500 mL.
Estimated concentration of secreted monoclonal antibody in the supernatant, measured on the collected fluid before purification; typical range is 0-200 ug/mL depending on hybridoma productivity.

Visual or instrument-assessed cleanliness of the collected supernatant before purification, reflecting presence of visible debris or turbidity; use to indicate whether the fluid was sufficiently clear for downstream processing.
Storage state of the harvested supernatant prior to purification, recorded as a material attribute of the entity; examples include 4 C short-term, -20 C, or -80 C long-term.
Indicates whether any preservative or antimicrobial additive was present in the collected supernatant before purification; true if additive was intentionally included, false otherwise.

purified_antibody_prep.reasoning: I corrected the purified_antibody_prep Entity schema by removing fields that collide with already_generated metadata across the DAG: antibody_isotype and storage_condition. I kept only prep-specific intrinsic attributes that still describe the purified material itself without drifting into purification process details or downstream assay outputs. The remaining fields focus on identity, provenance link, concentration, purity/aggregation, formulation, endotoxin, and QC status, which are appropriate for a purified material entity.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the purified antibody material lot or aliquot prepared for screening assays; example format: PAB-0001.
Identifier of the antibody supernatant lot from which this purified prep was derived, recorded as the material origin link; example format: SUP-0001.
Identifier for the monoclonal antibody clone represented by this purified prep, used to link the material to its producing hybridoma; example format: HBM-00123.
Measured antibody concentration in the purified preparation after purification and before screening assays; typical range is 0.01-20 mg/mL depending on yield and formulation.
Estimated percent purity of the purified antibody material, assessed on the prep before screening; typical range is 0-100 percent, with higher values indicating fewer contaminating proteins.
Estimated fraction of antibody present as higher-order aggregates in the purified prep, measured on the material before assay setup; typical range is 0-100 percent and lower values are preferred.

Formulation buffer used for the purified antibody preparation as it enters screening assays, described as the final material environment rather than the purification protocol; example formats include PBS, Tris-buffered saline, or PBS with 0.01 percent Tween-20.
Measured endotoxin content of the purified antibody preparation, assessed after purification and before functional assays when relevant; typical range is 0-100 EU/mg.
Indicates whether the purified antibody preparation met the laboratory's acceptance criteria for downstream screening assays, based on purity, concentration, and integrity checks.

cancer_cell_line.reasoning: For the cancer_cell_line entity, I kept only intrinsic cell-material fields describing identity, provenance, biology, and QC status before preparation. I excluded all process, capture, signal, and derivative information, as well as any fields that would duplicate previously generated identifiers or provenance terms. In particular, I removed species_origin because it already exists in prior DAG steps, and replaced it with a cell-line-specific provenance field. I also avoided repeating fields that could semantically overlap with earlier entity metadata such as source origin or storage-like attributes.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the cancer cell line or primary cancer cell culture used in the screening workflow; example format: CL-0001 or A549.

Original tumor, tissue, or disease source from which the cancer cell line was derived, recorded as an intrinsic provenance attribute of the culture; example values include breast tumor, lung tumor, melanoma lesion, or leukemia sample.
Cancer category represented by the cell line, used to describe the intrinsic biological context of the culture; examples include carcinoma, leukemia, lymphoma, melanoma, or sarcoma.

Relative expression level of the screening target antigen on the cancer cell line, measured or assigned for the cell material prior to assay preparation; typical categorical values are low, medium, high, or unknown.

Passage number of the cancer cell line at the time this entity is defined or banked for screening, reported as an intrinsic culture-state attribute; typical range is 1-200 depending on laboratory practice.

Whether the cancer cell line identity has been authenticated before use in the screening workflow, such as by STR profiling or equivalent confirmation; indicates material provenance quality rather than assay outcome.
Mycoplasma contamination status of the cancer cell line at the time of banking or definition, captured as a quality attribute of the cell material; categories reflect routine cell-culture QC.

Base growth medium typically used to maintain the cancer cell line before assay preparation, recorded as a material environment attribute rather than a preparation protocol; examples include RPMI 1640, DMEM, or IMDM.
Whether the cell line represents a master bank, working bank, actively cultured stock, or primary culture, indicating the preservation state of the entity rather than a handling step.

Broad morphological phenotype of the cancer cell line as observed in routine culture, recorded as a stable descriptive attribute of the entity; example values include adherent epithelial-like, suspension lymphoid-like, or fibroblast-like.

assay_ready_cells.reasoning: The assay_ready_cells node is an Entity, so I kept only intrinsic preparation-state attributes for the prepared cell material and avoided upstream cell-line provenance and downstream assay/capture outputs. I removed the colliding qc_passed field and retained unique fields that describe the prepared batch's identity, format, density, viability, and handling state. I also avoided repeating previously used provenance-style fields that were already assigned to earlier entity nodes.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the prepared cancer-cell batch or aliquot used in measurement workflows; example format: ARC-0001.
Identifier of the upstream cancer cell line from which these assay-ready cells were prepared, recorded as the provenance link to the parent entity; example format: CL-0001.
Date on which the cells were made assay-ready, such as plated, harvested, washed, counted, or suspended under assay conditions; ISO example: 2026-08-18.
Physical format of the assay-ready cells at the time of measurement setup; indicates whether cells were plated, in suspension, or embedded in another assay-compatible format.
Number of cells placed per well or equivalent assay unit when the prepared cells were plated; typical range is 100-1000000 cells per well depending on assay type.
Percent viable cells in the prepared batch immediately before assay start, measured after preparation and before capture; typical range is 0-100 percent.
Estimated percent surface coverage of adherent assay-ready cells at the time of measurement setup, recorded only for plated adherent cultures; typical range is 0-100 percent.
Final suspension or plating medium in which the assay-ready cells were maintained immediately before measurement; examples include complete RPMI 1640, DMEM, or PBS for short-term assay handling.
Type of plate, dish, or vessel containing the assay-ready cells at the time of measurement setup; example values include 96_well_plate, 24_well_plate, 384_well_plate, or culture_dish.
Duration for which cells were allowed to recover, adhere, or equilibrate after preparation and before measurement; typical range is 0-72 hours.

culture_collection.reasoning: The culture_collection node is a Process, so I included only how the supernatant harvesting was performed and the operational parameters that define the collection step itself. I excluded properties of the hybridoma culture, the resulting supernatant material, and any downstream purification details because those belong to the upstream Entity and downstream Entity/Process nodes. I also avoided the previously colliding field name qc_passed and did not repeat any sample identifiers that would be part of the material entities rather than the collection process.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the supernatant-harvesting operation performed on the hybridoma culture; example format: COL-0001.
Timestamp when the culture collection operation began, recorded at the start of harvesting from the hybridoma culture; ISO datetime example: 2026-08-18T09:30:00Z.
Timestamp when the collection operation was completed and the supernatant was separated from the culture; ISO datetime example: 2026-08-18T10:15:00Z.

Operational method used to harvest the antibody-containing culture fluid from the hybridoma culture, recorded as the collection approach rather than a property of the supernatant; typical values include centrifugation, aspiration, filtration, or clarification followed by decanting.
Relative centrifugal force used during clarification of the culture before or during collection, if applicable; typical range is 100-10000 x g.
Duration of the clarification or separation step used to obtain clean supernatant, measured during the collection process; typical range is 1-60 minutes.
Temperature at which the culture was collected and clarified, recorded during the harvesting operation; typical range is 0-37 Celsius depending on workflow requirements.
Indicates whether any anticoagulant, preservative, or collection additive was used during harvesting of the culture fluid; include only if intentionally applied during collection.
Volume of antibody-containing supernatant recovered by the collection operation, measured at the end of the process; typical range is 0.1-1000 mL.
Fraction of expected culture fluid recovered during collection relative to the planned harvest volume, reported as a process yield metric; typical range is 0-100 percent.
Identifier for the person or automated station responsible for the collection step, recorded for process traceability; example format: OP-07.

antibody_purification.reasoning: The antibody_purification node is a Process, so I included only the purification method, operating parameters, reagents/consumables, and process-level performance metrics that describe how the monoclonal antibodies were isolated from the collected culture material. I excluded intrinsic properties of the resulting purified prep, because those belong on the purified_antibody_prep Entity, and I excluded collection parameters and downstream assay setup because those belong to the culture_collection Process and later Capture nodes. I also avoided any field names already used in prior steps, including qc_passed, antibody_isotype, storage_condition, species_origin, and operator_id.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the antibody purification operation applied to hybridoma-derived culture material; example format: PUR-0001.
Identifier of the culture supernatant lot entering the purification step, used to trace the material processed by this operation; example format: SUP-0001.
Primary purification strategy used to isolate monoclonal antibodies from the culture material; report the method applied during this process step.
Name of the affinity matrix or chromatography resin used during purification, if applicable; example format: Protein A Sepharose, Protein G agarose, or equivalent.
Buffer composition used for antibody binding to the purification resin or matrix, recorded as a process reagent condition; example formats include PBS, Tris-HCl, or glycine-free binding buffer.
Buffer composition used to wash the purification matrix during the purification process, recorded for reproducibility of the operation.
Buffer composition used to elute antibodies from the purification matrix, recorded as a process reagent condition; example formats include glycine-HCl pH 2.7 or citrate buffer.
Measured or set pH of the elution buffer during antibody release from the purification matrix; typical range is 1.5-8.0 depending on method.
Temperature at which the purification operation was performed, measured during the process; typical range is 0-25 Celsius for most antibody workflows.
Total duration of the purification operation from sample loading to final pool collection, measured in minutes; typical range is 5-1440 minutes.
Estimated percentage of antibody recovered from the input material after purification, reported as a process outcome metric; typical range is 0-100 percent.
Name of any controlling or analysis software used to run, monitor, or record the purification workflow when an automated system is involved; example format: ChromLab or vendor control software.
Version of the purification control or monitoring software used during the process, recorded for reproducibility; example format: 5.0.1.
Repository, vendor source, or release reference for the software used in purification control or monitoring, when applicable; example format: vendor URL or Git repository reference.

cell_preparation.reasoning: The cell_preparation node is a Process, so I included only the operational parameters and handling details used to expand and prepare the cancer cells for downstream binding and functional assays. I excluded intrinsic cell-line attributes such as species, disease type, and antigen expression because those belong to the cancer_cell_line Entity, and I excluded assay readouts because those belong to Capture, Signal, or Derivative nodes. I also avoided the previously colliding field wash_buffer_composition and used process-specific preparation fields instead.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the cell expansion and preparation operation performed on the cancer cell line; example format: CP-0001.
Identifier of the cancer cell line entering the preparation step, used to trace the source material processed by this operation; example format: CL-0001.
Composition of the growth medium used to expand or maintain the cancer cells during preparation; example formats include RPMI 1640 with 10 percent FBS or DMEM with supplements.
List of supplements added during cell expansion or preparation, such as serum, antibiotics, glutamine, or growth factors, recorded at the process step level.
Temperature used during cell expansion or equilibration in the preparation step; typical range is 20-40 Celsius, most often 37 Celsius for mammalian cells.
Carbon dioxide percentage used during cell incubation for preparation, when cells are maintained in a controlled incubator; typical range is 0-10 percent and commonly 5 percent.
Duration of the cell expansion or equilibration period during preparation, measured from start to finish of the process; typical range is 0.5-168 hours.
Method used to harvest or detach cells during preparation, such as trypsinization, EDTA treatment, scraping, or direct collection of suspension cells.
Buffer or rinse solution used to wash cells during preparation before assay setup, recorded as a process reagent condition; example formats include PBS or HBSS.
Method used to count or estimate cell concentration during preparation, such as hemocytometer, automated counter, or imaging-based count.
Cell concentration achieved after preparation and before assay setup, measured in cells per milliliter; typical range is 1e3-1e8 cells/mL depending on assay format.
Percentage of expected viable cells recovered after the preparation process relative to the starting input, reported as a process outcome metric; typical range is 0-100 percent.
Free-text operational notes capturing any nonstandard handling, deviations, or observations during cell preparation that may affect downstream assay performance.

elisa_capture.reasoning: The elisa_capture node is a Capture step, so I included only the measurement-session and instrument-configuration fields needed to describe how the ELISA binding readout was acquired. This includes the plate reader identity, hardware configuration, acquisition settings, assay plate context, and controlled environmental conditions during capture. I excluded purified-antibody material properties, cell preparation details, and any raw file or downstream metric fields because those belong to upstream Entity nodes, the cell preparation Process, the ELISA Signal node, or the ELISA Derivative node. I also avoided the previously colliding field plate_type and did not repeat any process identifiers that have already been used elsewhere in the DAG.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the ELISA measurement session, recorded for the specific run that acquired the antibody binding signal; example format: ELISA-CAP-0001.
Manufacturer of the ELISA plate reader used for the capture session, recorded as the hardware source of the measurement; example values include Thermo Fisher, BioTek, Tecan, or Molecular Devices.
Model name or number of the plate reader used to capture the ELISA signal, recorded for instrument traceability; example format: SpectraMax iD3 or Synergy H1.
Serial number of the plate reader used for the ELISA capture session, recorded as the specific hardware identifier; example format: SN-123456.
Microplate format used for the ELISA capture session, configured on the instrument and used for signal acquisition; example values include 96_well_plate or 384_well_plate.
Optical read mode configured for the ELISA capture session, such as absorbance or luminescence, depending on the assay design.
Primary measurement wavelength used during ELISA signal acquisition, configured on the plate reader; typical range is 200-1000 nm depending on read mode.
Time used by the plate reader to integrate signal at each read point during ELISA capture; typical range is 1-10000 milliseconds.
Detector gain or sensitivity setting applied during the ELISA capture session, recorded as an instrument configuration parameter for reproducibility.
Temperature maintained during ELISA acquisition on the instrument or plate carrier, measured during the capture session; typical range is 4-37 Celsius.
Orbital shaking speed applied by the plate reader before or during reads, if enabled, recorded as an instrument setting affecting capture consistency; typical range is 0-2000 rpm.
Delay between plate loading and signal acquisition, measured during the capture session when the instrument waits before reading; typical range is 0-3600 seconds.
Identifier for the person or automated station that initiated and managed the ELISA capture session, recorded for session traceability; example format: OP-07.
Name of the instrument control software used to run the ELISA capture session; example format: SoftMax Pro or vendor plate-reader control software.
Version of the instrument control software used for ELISA acquisition, recorded for reproducibility; example format: 7.1.2.
Repository, vendor source, or release reference for the capture software used in the ELISA session; example format: vendor URL or Git repository reference.

flow_capture.reasoning: The flow_capture node is a Capture step, so I retained only flow-specific acquisition settings and session descriptors that do not collide with previously generated DAG fields. I excluded repeated generic instrument and software identifiers because they were already generated for earlier capture steps, and I avoided cell, antibody, signal, and derivative properties because those belong to other node types. The remaining fields describe the flow cytometry acquisition configuration that is specific to this measurement session.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the flow cytometry measurement session used to capture antibody binding events; example format: FLOW-CAP-0001.
Excitation laser wavelength used for flow cytometry acquisition, recorded as a capture setting; typical values include 405, 488, 561, or 640 nm.
Detector or fluorescence channel used for the antibody-binding readout during acquisition, recorded as the specific measurement channel.
Detector voltage or gain voltage applied during the flow acquisition session, recorded as an instrument setting for reproducibility; typical range is 200-1000 V depending on instrument.
Sample flow rate mode used during acquisition, recorded as a capture configuration; common settings include low, medium, or high.
Target number of events or cells collected during the flow cytometry session, recorded as an acquisition setting; typical range is 1000-1000000 events.
High-level gating scheme used during acquisition or live monitoring, recorded as the capture-time strategy for isolating relevant events; example values include singlets_live_cells or cells_only.
Indicates whether spectral compensation was applied during the capture session to correct fluorescence overlap; true if compensation matrices were loaded or used.
Temperature maintained during flow acquisition when the cytometer or sample chamber was controlled; typical range is 4-37 Celsius.

apoptosis_capture.reasoning: The apoptosis_capture node is a Capture step, so I included only the measurement session and instrument configuration needed to describe how the apoptosis readout was acquired after antibody treatment. This covers the assay device identity, detection configuration, acquisition parameters, and controlled session conditions specific to the capture event. I excluded treated-cell properties, antibody prep properties, raw file structure, and computed apoptosis metrics because those belong to Entity, upstream Process, Signal, or Derivative nodes. I also avoided repeating any fields already generated earlier in the DAG, including instrument_manufacturer, instrument_model, instrument_serial_number, capture_operator_id, capture_software_name, capture_software_version, capture_software_repository, integration_time_ms, gain_setting, and incubation_temperature_celsius.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the apoptosis measurement session used to acquire the treatment response signal; example format: APO-CAP-0001.

Type of platform used to capture apoptosis readout, such as a cell imaging system or plate reader, recorded at the session level; example values include microscopy-based imaging or luminescence reader.
Detection mode used during apoptosis capture, such as fluorescence, luminescence, or absorbance, depending on the assay chemistry; records the active readout mode during the session.
Excitation wavelength used for fluorescence-based apoptosis capture, if applicable; typical range is 350-700 nm depending on fluorophore.
Emission wavelength or detection band used for fluorescence-based apoptosis capture, if applicable; typical range is 400-800 nm depending on fluorophore.
Camera or detector exposure time used for imaging-based apoptosis capture, when a cell imaging system is used; typical range is 1-10000 milliseconds.
Time between antibody treatment and apoptosis measurement, recorded as the capture delay that defines when the signal was acquired; typical range is 0-168 hours depending on assay design.
Number of technical or biological replicate wells or fields acquired in the apoptosis capture session, recorded at the measurement stage; typical range is 1-100.
Named reagent or probe used to detect apoptotic cells during capture, such as Annexin V dye, caspase-sensitive fluorophore, or similar detection chemistry.
Indicates whether the capture platform maintained a controlled temperature during measurement, such as on-instrument warming or cooling; true if temperature regulation was active.

proliferation_capture.reasoning: The proliferation_capture node is a Capture step, so I included only capture-session and instrument-setting fields that have not already been used elsewhere in the DAG. These fields describe how the proliferation measurement was acquired, including session identity, timing, scanning configuration, detection chemistry, and acquisition-specific controls. I excluded treated-cell attributes, raw files, and computed proliferation outputs because those belong to Entity, upstream Process, Signal, or Derivative nodes. I also removed fields that collided with previously generated capture-step metadata such as assay_platform, assay_read_mode, exposure_time_ms, replicate_count, and capture_temperature_controlled.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the proliferation measurement session used to acquire the treatment response signal; example format: PRO-CAP-0001.
Time point after antibody treatment at which proliferation was measured, recorded as the capture timing relative to treatment start; typical range is 0-240 hours depending on assay design.
Named reagent or probe used to detect proliferating cells during capture, such as DNA synthesis markers, metabolic dyes, or fluorescence proliferation indicators.

Order in which wells or fields were read during the proliferation capture session, recorded for acquisition traceability when scan sequence matters; example values include row_major, column_major, or randomized.
Indicates whether background subtraction or correction was applied at acquisition time for the proliferation readout; true if the capture workflow performed instrument-side correction.

Spatial scan pattern used by the imaging or reader instrument during proliferation acquisition, recorded when acquisition traverses multiple fields or wells; example values include serpentine, raster, or center_out.
Number of fields of view or measurement positions collected per well or sample during the proliferation capture session; typical range is 1-1000.
Indicates whether autofocus was active during the proliferation capture session, relevant for imaging-based acquisition to maintain sharpness at each field; true if autofocus was used.
Mode used to set imaging exposure during proliferation acquisition, such as fixed exposure or adaptive exposure, recorded to describe capture behavior without repeating numeric exposure time fields.
Free-text notes describing any capture-time environmental factors or operational remarks relevant to the proliferation session, such as humidity, vibration, or interruptions.

elisa_signal.reasoning: The elisa_signal node is a Signal, so I included only raw data artefact properties: file identity, format, size, dimensionality, channel/layout details, acquisition matrix shape, and technical quality/storage attributes of the ELISA readout itself. I excluded capture settings, antibody prep properties, assay interpretation, and downstream metrics because those belong to the Capture, Entity, or Derivative nodes. I also avoided any fields already generated earlier in the DAG, including plate_type and instrument/capture-specific names. The fields are specific to the raw ELISA artefact and are sufficient for downstream parsing and reuse.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw ELISA data artefact produced by the capture session; example format: ELISA-SIG-0001.
Identifier of the ELISA capture session that produced this raw signal, recorded as the provenance link from measurement session to data artefact; example format: ELISA-CAP-0001.
Name of the raw ELISA data file as stored by the acquisition system; example format: elisa_run_001.gel or assay_readout.xml.
File format of the raw ELISA output artefact, recorded at the data layer; common values depend on instrument export such as csv, xlsx, xml, txt, or proprietary instrument format.
Size of the raw ELISA data file in bytes, measured after acquisition and before any analysis processing; typical range is 1000 to 100000000 bytes depending on plate size and export format.
Number of wells represented in the raw ELISA signal file, recorded as a dimensionality attribute of the artefact; typical values are 1-1536 depending on plate format.
Number of raw measurement points or readouts contained in the ELISA artefact, such as single endpoint values or repeated reads over time; typical range is 1-100000.
Matrix dimensions of the ELISA data as exported, reported as rows by columns or an equivalent encoded shape string; example format: 8x12 for a 96-well plate.
List or encoded summary of wavelengths present in the raw ELISA artefact, measured in nanometers and captured directly from the instrument output; typical values depend on assay read mode.
Indicates whether the raw ELISA file already contains blank-subtracted values at the data-export level; true only if subtraction was applied before the file was saved.
Technical quality flag assigned to the raw ELISA artefact based on export completeness, obvious corruption, or unreadable wells; use only data-technical categories, not biological interpretation.
Primary storage path, bucket, database, or repository location where the raw ELISA artefact is kept; example format: s3://bucket/path/file.csv or /data/run001/ elisa.csv.
Checksum for the raw ELISA data file used to verify integrity and detect corruption or changes after acquisition; example format: 32-character hexadecimal MD5 string.

flow_signal.reasoning: The flow_signal node is a Signal, so I included only raw data artefact properties that are specific to the flow event file and have not been used in earlier DAG steps. I focused on technical structure, event/channel counts, file layout, and data-quality indicators needed for parsing and integrity checks. I excluded capture settings, gating interpretation, antibody or cell properties, and derived metrics because those belong to upstream Capture/Entity nodes or downstream analysis nodes. I also avoided the previously colliding raw-file fields source_capture_session_id, file_name, file_format, file_size_bytes, storage_location, and checksum_md5 by choosing alternative artefact descriptors.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw flow cytometry data artefact produced by the capture session; example format: FLOW-SIG-0001.
Total number of flow events recorded in the raw artefact, measured directly from the event file; typical range is 1000-100000000 events.
Number of fluorescence and scatter channels contained in the raw flow file, recorded as an artefact dimensionality attribute; typical range is 1-64 channels.
List of channel or parameter names encoded in the raw flow data file, such as FSC-A, SSC-A, FITC-A, or APC-A, captured directly from the event file header.
Total time span covered by the recorded events in the raw flow artefact, measured from first to last event timestamp; typical range is 0-86400 seconds.
Indicates whether forward scatter and side scatter channels are present in the raw flow file; true if FSC/SSC parameters were exported with the artefact.
Indicates whether fluorescence intensity channels are present in the raw flow file; true if one or more labeled detector channels were exported.
Indicates whether the raw flow artefact preserves the acquisition order of events as exported from the instrument; true if event sequence is retained.
Technical quality flag assigned to the raw flow artefact based on file completeness, event integrity, or importability; use only data-technical categories, not biological interpretation.
Encoded dimensionality of the raw flow artefact, such as number of events by number of parameters, recorded as a compact shape string; example format: 50000x18.
Byte offset or technical header position reported by the raw flow export, used for file parsing and low-level validation when available; typical range is 0 to 1000000 bytes.

apoptosis_signal.reasoning: The apoptosis_signal node is a Signal, so I included only raw data artefact properties: file identity, format, size, dimensionality, channel/image structure, and technical quality/storage attributes of the apoptosis assay output itself. I excluded capture settings, treatment conditions, biological interpretation, and computed apoptosis metrics because those belong to Capture, Process/Entity, or Derivative nodes. I also avoided any fields already generated earlier in the DAG, including source_capture_session_id, file_name, file_format, file_size_bytes, storage_location, and checksum_md5, and kept the fields specific to the raw apoptosis artefact so downstream users can locate and parse the data.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the raw apoptosis assay data artefact produced by the capture session; example format: APO-SIG-0001.
Identifier of the apoptosis capture session that produced this raw signal, recorded as the provenance link from measurement session to artefact; example format: APO-CAP-0001.
Name of the raw apoptosis data artefact as stored by the acquisition system; example format: apoptosis_run_001.csv or image_stack_01.tif.
File or export format of the raw apoptosis output artefact, recorded at the data layer; common values depend on platform and may include csv, tiff, png, txt, or raw export.
Number of assay fields, wells, images, or time frames represented in the raw apoptosis artefact, measured directly from the exported data object; typical range is 1-100000 depending on assay design.
Dimensionality of the raw apoptosis artefact, such as pixel dimensions for images or rows by columns for tabular output; example formats include 1024x1024 or 8x12.
List of image channels or signal channels present in the raw apoptosis artefact, captured directly from the export metadata; example values include DAPI, FITC, caspase channel, or brightfield.
Bit depth or numeric precision of the raw apoptosis data export, measured at the artefact level; typical values are 8, 12, 16, or 32 bits depending on platform.
Native numeric range or intensity units represented in the raw apoptosis artefact, recorded as an export-level technical property; example values include arbitrary fluorescence units or counts.
Technical quality flag assigned to the raw apoptosis artefact based on completeness, corruption, saturation, or missing frames; use only data-technical categories, not biological interpretation.
Primary storage path, bucket, database, or repository location where the raw apoptosis artefact is kept; example format: s3://bucket/path/apoptosis_run_001.tif or /data/run001/apoptosis.csv.

Checksum for the raw apoptosis data file used to verify integrity and detect corruption or changes after acquisition; example format: 32-character hexadecimal MD5 string or equivalent checksum string.

proliferation_signal.reasoning: The candidate_ranking node is a Derivative, so I included only computed-result fields that describe the integrated prioritization output itself: the ranking table identity, scoring method, contributing metric weights, rank position, selected lead status, and quality indicators of the computed result. I excluded upstream assay details, capture settings, raw signal file properties, and process parameters because those belong to Entity, Process, Capture, or Signal nodes. I also avoided repeating any previously generated field names, including those from raw signal nodes and prior assay steps, and kept the schema focused on the final integrated candidate-selection output.

md_schema.descr: Unique identifier for the computed lead-candidate ranking result table produced by the integrative selection step; example format: RANK-0001.
Identifier for the collection of assay metric tables used as input to the ranking computation, linking the derivative result to its source metrics; example format: METRICS-SET-0001.

Name of the algorithm, rule set, or scoring framework used to compute the final antibody ranking; example values include weighted_sum, z_score_composite, rule_based_priority, or machine_learning_model.
Version or release identifier of the ranking algorithm or scoring framework used to produce the candidate priorities; example format: 1.0.3 or v2.1.
Description of how ELISA, flow cytometry, apoptosis, and proliferation metrics were weighted in the final ranking calculation; record the weighting scheme applied to the input metrics.
Method used to normalize input metric values before ranking, such as z-score, min-max scaling, percentile ranking, or none; captures the computational transformation applied to inputs.
